questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=-5 \\ 2x+3y=5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=3 \\ 2x-y=5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5x=1-3y \\ 3-4y=2x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5x+3y=1 \\ -2x-4y=-3.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot (-4)-(-2)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=4 \\ x=-2y-1\end{aligned}
$$

First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-y=4 \\ x+2y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x=-3y \\ 2x=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+3y=0 \\ 2x=3.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 0-3\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find a solution to the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+y=2 \\ 4x+3y=6.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the solution is $x=0$ and $y=2.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 6y-5x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $A\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -5 & 6\end{aligned}]$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot 2-3\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=-3.$
